As a and $\mathrm{b}$ have same stopping potential and $\mathrm{c}$ has greater stopping potential, then $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{c}} > \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{a}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{b}}$ as $\mathrm{b}$ and $\mathrm{c}$ have same saturation current and $a$ has lesser value.

questions.q: Photons of energy $2.4 \mathrm{eV}$ and wavelength $\lambda$ fall on a metal plate and release photoelectrons with a maximum velocity $v$. By decreasing $\lambda$ by $50 \%$, the maximum velocity of photoelectrons becomes $3 v$. The work function of the material of the metal plate is
questions.solution:
Let $\phi_0=$ work-function of metal.
Then, according to Einstein's photoelectric equation, $K_{\max }=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{h c}{\lambda}-\phi_0$ When wavelength is reduced by $50 \%$ i.e, $\lambda^{\prime}=\frac{\lambda}{2}$, then maximum velocity of emitted electrons is $3 v$.
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we have $\begin{aligned} & 9\left(\frac{h c}{\lambda}-\phi_0\right)=\frac{2 h c}{\lambda}-\phi_0 \\ & 7 \frac{h c}{\lambda}=8 \phi_0 \Rightarrow \phi_0=\frac{7}{8} \frac{h c}{\lambda} \end{aligned}$ Here, photon energy is given as $\frac{h c}{\lambda}=2.4 \mathrm{eV}$ So, work-function is $\phi_0=\frac{7}{8} \times 2.4=2.1 \mathrm{eV}$

For perfectly elastic collision,

$u = {v}_{y} - {v}_{x}... \left(ii\right)$

Force on electron in electric field,

$F = - eE = - e\left[- {E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}\right] = e{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}$

Acceleration of electron, $a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{e{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}}{m}$
Velocity of electron after time $t$,

$

$⇒$ So, $\dfrac{{E}_{A}}{{E}_{B}} = \dfrac{1}{K^{2}}\left(or\right){E}_{A}: {E}_{B} = 1: K^{2}$

According to the equation of photoelectric effect,

$K{E}_\max = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - {ϕ}_{0}$

$\dfrac{p^{2}}{2m} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - {ϕ}_{0}$

$\dfrac{d{\lambda}_{d}}{d\lambda} ∝ \dfrac{{\lambda}_d^{3}}{{\lambda}^{2}}$

$\dfrac{{E}_{A}}{{E}_{B}} = \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{{U}_{A}}{{U}_{B}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

And ${E}_{B} = {U}_{B} + {K}_{B}$

here ${K}_{A}$ and ${K}_{B}$ are kinetic energy of particles $A$ and $B$

So ${K}_{A} = {E}_{A} - {U}_{A} = \left(x - y\right)$ .....(i)

From Equation (i), (ii) and (iii),

$\dfrac{{\lambda}_{A}}{{\lambda}_{B}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(x - y\right)}{\left(x - y\right)}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{1}$

questions.q: An electron (mass $m$ ) with initial velocity $\overset{→}{v} = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j}$ is in an electric filed $\overset{→}{E} = - {E}_{0}\overset{^}{k}.$ If ${\lambda}_{0}$ is initial de-Broglie wavelength of electron, its de-Broglie wave length at time $t$ is given by:

Initial velocity of electron,&

$v = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j} ⇒ \left|u\right| = \sqrt{{v}_{0}^{2} + {v}_{0}^{2}} = {v}_{0}\sqrt{2}$

Initial de Broglie wavelength associated with electron,

${λ}_{0} = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{m{v}_{0}\sqrt{2}}$

now,

$v = u + at$
Velocity as a function of time $= {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{e{E}_{0}}{m}t\overset{^}{k}$
so wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m\sqrt{2{v}_{0}^{2} + \dfrac{e^{2}{E}_{0}^{2}}{m^{2}}t^{2}}}$
$\lambda = \dfrac{{\lambda}_{0}}{\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{e^{2}{E}_{0}^{2}}{2m^{2}{v}_{0}^{2}}t^{2}}}$
